## A running example

This is a template: it runs nowhere itself. A system started from it is running at [https://ultrastable-seed-second-tenant.ultrastable.workers.dev](https://ultrastable-seed-second-tenant.ultrastable.workers.dev/) (repository [ultrastable/second-tenant](https://github.com/ultrastable/second-tenant), health report at [https://ultrastable-seed-second-tenant.ultrastable.workers.dev/health](https://ultrastable-seed-second-tenant.ultrastable.workers.dev/health)).

Every system running on Ultrastable is listed at [https://ultrastable.io/directory](https://ultrastable.io/directory).
<!-- example:end -->


**Ultrastable is the foundation for any autonomous system.**

A system is autonomous if it has self-referential loops and the ability to close them. Knowing without being able to act is useless, so the system is privileged to close its own loops (`python3 -m foundation loops --verify`).

Ultrastable runs on itself: its roadmap, issues, managers, trust ledger, plussing budget and specs are run by the same code it gives everyone else, from this repository alone, with any tools (`python3 -m foundation selfhost`).

The spark. One person writes an idea; this repo turns it into a running organization of virtual managers and staff, server-side, on a heartbeat.

```
IDEA.md  ──►  bootstrap/bootstrap.py  ──►  org/ (charter, roles, backlog, gate cards)
                                      ──►  D1 schema + seed rows
                                      ──►  Worker with a 10-minute tick (managers run here)
```

After the first boot, nothing runs on a laptop. The bootstrapper is the only step that starts from a person; every later step starts from the tick.

## Start with an idea (no code, no terminal, no key)

What you do:

1. Press **Use this template** on this page. That gives you your own copy.
2. In your copy, open **Issues** and choose **Start my system**. Say in a sentence or two what it should do and keep doing. That is all.

What the system does, by itself, from there:

- It writes [`IDEA.md`](IDEA.md) from your words and fills in the rest (the loop it closes, its first measure, a small monthly budget) so the managers can start; they replace the measure once the first readings exist (`bootstrap/intake.py`).
- It plans the organization (charter, roles, backlog, checks), tests itself and simulates a year unattended (`bootstrap/bootstrap.py`, run by [`bootstrap.yml`](.github/workflows/bootstrap.yml) on the server).
- It deploys itself when the repository has a hosting sign-in. When it has none, the plan is kept, the start is tried again every day, and you get one link that runs it on Ultrastable's own account with nothing to set up.
- It tells you what happened in plain words on one thread in your copy, **Your system**, and keeps that note current. A failure says what happened and what the system is doing about it; none of them hands you a task.

A missing sign-in never stops the boot. The step is recorded as a backlog item with its blocker and a closing probe, each thing only you can approve is one card with one link and a default in effect, and the rest of the boot continues (the AIOS "PID 1 never dies" rule; see [docs/bootstrapping.md](docs/bootstrapping.md)).

Engineers: the same boot runs anywhere with Python 3.11+ (`bootstrap/bootstrap.py --dry-run` plans and writes `org/`, `--apply` also deploys when the environment holds the hosting sign-in). Nobody has to.

## What is in the seed

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`IDEA.md`](IDEA.md) | The idea, the person, the first outcomes. The one human input. |
| [`ultrastable.json`](ultrastable.json) | Org config: name, roles, connectors, model ladder, budget, capacity rules. Defaults work as-is. |
| [`autonomy/policy.json`](autonomy/policy.json) | Autonomy settings: the maximum permission per surface, action classes, trust ladder defaults and thresholds, the narrow interrupt gate, standing limits. |
| [`agents/AGENTS.md`](agents/AGENTS.md) | The shared protocol every agent reads (Claude Code, Copilot, Codex, any other). |
| [`agents/roles/`](agents/roles/) | One instruction file per virtual role: portfolio, project, product manager, staff, reviewer, operations. |
| [`.claude/settings.json`](.claude/settings.json) | Claude Code permissions at the ceiling the policy allows, with the gated actions denied. |
| [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md), [`.github/copilot-instructions.md`](.github/copilot-instructions.md) | Pointers so each agent loads `agents/AGENTS.md`. |
| [`bootstrap/bootstrap.py`](bootstrap/bootstrap.py) | The bootstrapper: read, detect, select, plan, provision, start, report. Stdlib only, idempotent. |
| [`worker/`](worker/) | The server-side runtime: Cloudflare Worker with the tick, D1 migrations, tests. |
| [`plugins/`](plugins/SCOPE.json) | Optional plugin tier (email, mailing list, social, YouTube, GCP, self-description, guided communication flow). Dry-run by default, never in the core path. Spec: `docs/architecture/plugins.md`. |
| [`tests/`](tests/) | Bootstrapper and policy tests, <!-- claim:seed-py-tests -->129<!-- /claim --> in all (`python3 -m unittest discover tests`). |
| [`docs/bootstrapping.md`](docs/bootstrapping.md) | The boot sequence, stage by stage, and what each stage learned from AIOS. |

## Rules the seed carries into every org it starts

- **Words match code (CLAIMS-1).** Every public statement is a probed sentence, a block generated from code, or an inventory checked in reverse (`doctrine/claims.json`; `python3 scripts/claims.py --check` on every change, `--fix` rewrites generated blocks, `--file` files one item per drift). A new claim is registered in the same change that makes it.
- **If it is not in code, it does not exist.** Every output of every role is a commit, an issue or a database row. Chat is never the record.
- **The fleet is the actor.** People set direction and take only identity-bound steps (money, signing, credentials only they hold, their own accounts). Each of those is a gate card, never an instruction in prose.
- **Narrow interrupt gate.** An agent stops only for a step that is irreversible and identity-bound with no reversible path. Everything else runs, is verified and reported.
- **Trust is computed, not granted.** It rises and falls with recorded outcomes per surface and action class, and widens scope only through a reviewed change to `autonomy/policy.json`.
- **Never self-review.** A different agent or model verifies each claimed result.
- **Plussing.** 20% of capacity goes to improvements, and every closed item proposes one.

## Interview and screens (no code needed)
`python3 bootstrap/interview.py --org-name "My Project"` asks plain questions with hints and numbered choices, then writes `IDEA.md` and `specs/`. The Worker serves the same interview at `/start` and three screens at `/`, `/next`, `/needs-you`. See [SCOPE.md](SCOPE.md) and [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md).

## How this system runs

**What it is.** The code-only kernel a new autonomous system starts from: bootstrapper, tick Worker, roles, agent instructions and the loops that take it to criticality. A copy of seed/ in the Ultrastable platform.

**The loop it closes.** Every tick the system reconciles its state, takes its highest-priority item, does it, verifies it through an independent path, scores the prediction it logged and files the next improvement.

**How it bootstraps.** One file, `IDEA.md`, states the idea and its system test (a loop to close, a measure that can be wrong, upkeep that never ends, a running cost the owner accepts). `bootstrap/bootstrap.py` reads it with `ultrastable.json` and `autonomy/policy.json`, qualifies the idea, hires the roles, writes the Worker's configuration and database, and deploys the tick Worker. No person runs a command.

**How it becomes autonomous.** Two ladders, both computed from evidence the system records, never declared:

- ignition (read every tick, reported at `/health`): `unseeded` → `seeded` → `ticking` → `looping` → `closing` → `instrumented` → `critical` → `self-sustaining`. `instrumented` and above means bootstrapped; the first unmet stage is filed as its own work item.
- lifecycle (`scripts/seedlife.py`): `seeded` → `planned` → `built` → `deployed` → `live` → `autonomous`. Stage at the last reading: `unmeasured`. `autonomous` needs every one-year survival question answered (credentials, budget, dependencies, models, health, backups, renewal, improvement, privacy).

**How criticality is read.** k = verified deploys / (normalized cost + human touches), logged every tick and served at `/live` (`k_eff`, and `k_self` for deploys the system originated itself). At or above 1 with `k_self` carrying it, the system is self-sustaining.
<!-- how:end -->
